skills.name: Nouns, pronouns and verbs in context

note.text: A noun can head a noun phrase; a pronoun can stand as the head of a noun phrase and refer to a person, thing or idea. A verb heads the predicate and can express an action, event or state. Form alone is insufficient: record is a noun in the record and a verb in record the decision. Pronoun references need to be clear. A sentence can contain several verb forms with different functions.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to identify a word’s function in its sentence and maintain clear reference. Builds on: Form Five parts of speech. Leads to: modification, determiners and sentence control.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: A noun can head a noun phrase; a pronoun can stand as the head of a noun phrase and refer to a person, thing or idea. A verb heads the predicate and can express an action, event or state. Form alone is insufficient: record is a noun in the record and a verb in record the decision. Pronoun references need to be clear. A sentence can contain several verb forms with different functions.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: Bih keeps the club record. She records decisions after meetings. Record follows the and heads a noun phrase in the first sentence; records is the finite verb in the second. She refers to Bih. If another possible person intervenes, repeating a name may be clearer than leaving a pronoun ambiguous.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Locate the whole phrase and clause before labelling a word. Ask what it does here. Track the intended referent and test whether a reader could reasonably identify someone else.

cards.idea: Read the whole example before identifying its function.
example: The record is complete uses record as a noun.
Bih checked the record; she corrected it.
Bih records decisions has records as its finite verb.
The record seems complete uses seems for a state.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Record must be the same word class in every sentence. Correction: Sentence position and function distinguish its uses.
A pronoun can never be unclear. Correction: Several possible referents can create ambiguity.
Every word ending in s is a plural noun. Correction: Records functions as a verb in this clause.
Every verb must describe a physical action. Correction: Verbs can express states as well as actions.

pick.q: In The club will record the decision, what is record doing?
pick.r: Functioning as a verb after will
w: Heading a noun phrase after the
Replacing the club as a pronoun
Describing a noun as an adjective
e: It follows the auxiliary will, not the determiner the.
It does not replace a referent.
It names the predicated action.
pick.y: Function in the clause determines the label.

pick.q: Bih told Ngozi that she had the key. Without further context, what may need clarification?
w: Whether the sentence has any verb
e: Key is explicit.
That relationship is explicit.
Told and had are verb forms.
pick.y: Both named people could be possible referents.

pick.q: In The room seems quiet, why is seems a verb?
pick.r: It heads a predicate expressing a state
w: Only action words can ever be verbs
It is the name of the room
Every word before an adjective is a noun
e: Verbs can express states.
Room names the place.
Position alone does not justify that rule.
pick.y: A state can be predicated without physical movement.
